positions.statement: Hill says residents should have more influence on how the city develops than outside entities, and that she endorsed Measure 3-632.
positions.excerpt: Residents should have more influence on how our city develops than outside entities, which is why I endorsed Measure 3-632.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 58, printed C-57)

positions.statement: Hill says city government should remove barriers, streamline processes, invest in infrastructure and be a trusted partner to business.
positions.excerpt: City government should remove barriers, streamline processes, invest wisely in infrastructure, and be a trusted partner to business.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 58, printed C-57)

positions.statement: Hill says that before asking residents for more money or taking on debt, the city must show responsible stewardship of what it has.
positions.excerpt: Before asking residents for more money or taking on debt, we must demonstrate responsible stewardship of what we already have.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 58, printed C-57)

positions.statement: In a joint pamphlet argument with Katie Dunwell on Measure 3-641, Hill says they are voting no on the Town Center urban renewal financing plan.
positions.excerpt: We are voting no on the Town Center urban renewal financing plan.
